why: LANDED (issue 1978): `nros::Node` and `nros::LifecycleNode` forward this to the executor that owns them, over `nros_cpp_executor_count_clients`. rclcpp (Jazzy) has `Node::count_clients`; Humble's rclcpp does not, which is why the Humble run reads it ours-only and this row carries no `editions`. It stays a divergence on SHAPE, as `cpp:Node::count_publishers`: `Result count_clients(const char*, size_t*)` rather than a returned `size_t`, so UNSUPPORTED (a backend with no graph) stays distinct from 0. The count reflects what has been DISCOVERED and never blocks.
